title: Per-request cost-aware retry and resume contract for chunked uploads and streaming responses
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Current cross-SDK retry defaults are agnostic to request cost and streaming posture. Heavy requests (large prompt/embedding inputs, chunked file uploads or long-running streaming generation) can incur significant billable work when retries happen blindly. We need a contract that lets SDKs make safer retry decisions per-request by combining idempotency semantics, per-chunk resume tokens, and a lightweight client-side cost heuristic.

Goal: Define a cross-language contract and reference implementation that: 1) classifies retryability for requests that may be high-cost or resumable, 2) standardizes on 'resume tokens' for resumable/chunked uploads and long-lived streams, 3) suggests conservative defaults for backoff that account for estimated work already performed, and 4) provides clear telemetry knobs and opt-outs for customers sensitive to cost.

Why unique: Instead of only keying retries by error class and idempotency key, this RFC ties retry decisions to request metadata (estimated token count, chunk index, stream posture) and defines resume semantics so SDKs can safely attempt resume or fall back without duplicate high-cost work.
acceptance_criteria: Cross-SDK spec doc published with exact header/field names for resume tokens and cost hints
Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs implement a CostAwareRetryPolicy with feature-flag toggle
End-to-end integration test covering chunked upload resume and streaming resume with simulated partial work and duplicate suppression
Telemetry events emitted: retry_decision, resume_attempt, duplicate_suppressed with payload-size and estimated_cost
Benchmarks showing <10% increased latency for small requests and >30% reduction in billable duplicate tokens for large/resumable requests compared to naive retries
decision_log: 2026-02-29: Choose header name 'X-RW-Resume-Token' for resumable operations to be orthogonal to SDKs and compatible with proxies
2026-02-29: Use 'X-RW-Cost-Estimate' header with integer estimated_token_count; SDKs populate conservatively (round up) from local prompt/attachment size heuristics
2026-03-02: Default policy: conservative backoff for estimated_cost > 1k tokens (base 1s, max 30s, jitter), permissive backoff for <100 tokens
2026-03-05: Opted NOT to force server-side dedup of all large operations; prefer client resume-first approach with server-side idempotency hints when available to reduce storage burden
2026-03-10: Resume token TTL: server recommends 24h; SDKs will surface retry window to users and expose a resume_expiry in SDK errors
progress_updates: 2026-03-04: Cross-team sync with Runtime and Console to validate resume-header parsing at edge and observability needs; Runtime requested structured telemetries for resume attempts
2026-03-07: Python reference implementation PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/481 (proto, tests, flaky on CI due to race - investigating)
2026-03-09: TS and Go stubs created in monorepo; TS team proposed using Fetch/AbortController ergonomics for streaming resume
2026-03-11: Review feedback from Security: ensure resume tokens are cryptographically random and scoped per-tenant; runtime to require signature HMAC when private deployment=true
2026-03-13: Updated spec to include header fallbacks for proxies and added explicit telemetry keys (retry_reason, estimated_tokens)
Pending: finalize API ergonomics for embedding customers who batch thousands of small records (edge case: treat batch of many small items as high-cost when total tokens > threshold)
implementation_notes: Python: implement CostAwareRetry as subclass of existing RetryPolicy; expose client.config.retry_cost_threshold and .resume_enabled boolean
TypeScript: provide a middleware for fetch-based and XHR-based clients; expose onRequest metadata with estimatedTokens(), chunkIndex optional and auto-populate X-RW- headers
Go: add RetryContext to request struct; provide utilities to compute conservative token estimate from bytes and model family; use context.Context values to thread resume_token
All SDKs: default behavior should be backwards-compatible (no headers added unless SDK computes estimate or resume token exists), feature-flag for experiment rollout
Server: add ephemeral resume token verifier and optional 'resume_allowed' flag in 409/308 style responses when resume possible
Testing: use chaos harness to simulate partial work completion, server crash between chunks, and network partitions to validate resume and duplicate suppression
tradeoffs_and_risks: Risk: Incorrect cost heuristics could under- or over-estimate; mitigation: default to conservative (treat unknown as high-cost) and expose opt-out
Tradeoff: Adding headers increases surface area for proxies/CDNs; we chose short, namespaced headers and provided fallback in request body for systems that strip headers
Risk: Resume tokens add storage/TTL burden on server; mitigation: recommend small token payloads (opaque ID with server-side metadata) and 24h TTL by default
Tradeoff: Server-side dedup would perfectly prevent duplicates but is expensive; client-first resume reduces server load at cost of more complex SDK logic
qa_plan: Unit tests: policy state transitions, header emission, and opt-out behavior across languages
Integration tests: chunked upload scenario with server returning 5xx mid-chunk, verify resume_attempt and no duplicate billing tokens
Load test: synthetic 10k concurrent resumable uploads with random failures to validate resume token throughput and server storage TTL cleanup
Canary rollout: enable policy for 5% of traffic on hosted API with additional logging and dashboard in Console to monitor duplicate token rate
